messages.subject: Methodology question re: hierarchical SEM
parts:
Evening all, 

I have a very complex dataset for which I have been advised I need to run an SEM. My problem is that I have not found any approaches that would allow for a hierarchical structure (e.g., lavaan requires no nesting or random effects). 
I will start with a very simple description, and elaborate as needed. 

Types of data: 
1) Vegetation - functional group by percent cover, vertical cover (height), bare ground (%), litter (%)
2) Rodents - counts of unique captures, standardized by trapping effort
3) Snakes - counts of individuals, standardized by survey effort
4) Raptors - counts of individuals, standardized by survey effort
(It's a lot more complex than that, and the sample unit varies for each parameter, but I am not sure how much information is needed at this stage)

Other variables: 
Location - we collected data at 4 locations (random effect)
Sites - there were 2 different site types within each of the 4 locations
Seasons - we collected data across 4 seasons

What we would like to do is somehow model the relationships between the four types of data, while accounting for site/location/season (if we don't account for these, I imagine we won't see anything interesting, but I could be wrong, because things like vegetation may help explain other trophic level responses more than "site type", but I am not sure). 

Any leads or guidance would be greatly appreciated. 

Happy Holidays!

parts:
Hi Kristina,

I can't help with the details of your study right now, but there are ways to incorporate hierarchical structure in SEM, based on methods made available by Bill Shipley.

Check out the following resources:

http://jonlefcheck.net/2014/07/06/piecewise-structural-equation-modeling-in-ecological-research/

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/piecewiseSEM/README.html

Shipley 2009 Ecology - sorry, couldn't get link easily

Shipley 2013 Ecology

Best,

Matt
